headline: Funding flows. Satellites shrink. Competitions heat up.
deck: Investments surge while satellite ambitions dwindle amidst rising competition.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190M in Series C funding, emphasizing its focus on co-orbital security and space domain awareness. This round underscores the Department of Defense's push for advanced capabilities in the face of increasing threats. With a valuation of $1.6B, True Anomaly is positioning itself as a key player in the defense tech space.
stories.soWhat: It's clear that the defense sector is betting heavily on co-orbital tech, likely out of a mix of paranoia and necessity.

stories.head: SES and Eutelsat cancel GEO expansion plans
stories.body: SES and Eutelsat have both scrapped their plans for new GEO expansion satellites, a move that highlights the tightening of satellite real estate and the challenges of profitability in the sector. This decision follows a broader trend of cost-cutting and strategic reevaluation among satellite operators. With less competition for orbital slots, the implications for future launches could be significant.
stories.soWhat: Sometimes less really is more, but in this case, it might just be a sign that the GEO market is becoming a graveyard.

stories.head: Anduril and L3Harris team up for SDA constellation
stories.body: Anduril and L3Harris are collaborating on a tactical Space Development Agency constellation bid, aiming to enhance U.S. space capabilities. This partnership reflects a growing trend of private-public collaboration in defense, as companies seek to leverage each other's strengths for competitive advantage. The exact funding details remain under wraps, but the stakes are high.
stories.soWhat: When two heavyweights team up, it’s usually a sign that they smell blood in the water—or at least a lucrative contract.

watchlist.title: SpaceX's Starship version 3 launch date
watchlist.body: With a launch date set, all eyes will be on whether SpaceX can finally deliver on its promises or if this will just be another date on the calendar.

watchlist.title: Northrop Grumman's lunar navigation system debut
watchlist.body: The LR-450 lunar navigation system could change the game for lunar missions, but its success hinges on real-world performance, not just PowerPoint presentations.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension
watchlist.body: Palantir's $480M extension on the TITAN program indicates strong demand for their ground station capabilities, but the real test will be execution.

watchlist.title: FY27 budget implications for space resilience
watchlist.body: With an additional $1.4B earmarked for space resilience, expect a flurry of proposals and maybe a few more 'urgent' meetings in the coming weeks.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.

Northrop Grumman's new lunar navigation system could be a game-changer, but investors will want to see solid contracts.
Palantir's extension on the TITAN program signals confidence in its capabilities, though skepticism remains about long-term growth.
